data.name: gasbillingperiod.hint.overview
data.value: Set the gas-bill start/end dates for each billing period (month); periods without custom settings default to starting the day after the previous period ends, lasting one month (calendar month if nothing is customized). Changes take effect immediately — all monthly gas views (Gas Usage Report / Gas Cost Report / EMS gas meter cards) are split by billing period, and historical monthly reports are recalculated with the new settings.

data.name: gasbillingperiod.hint.independent
data.value: This page affects gas usage and gas cost only. The gas utility reads meters on different dates than the power and water utilities, so all three billing cycles are configured independently — changes here do not affect electricity or water periods.

data.name: gasbillingperiod.hint.bimonthly
data.value: Two-month cycle: click "Delete Period" on a period and it disappears, with its days merged into the previous period (or absorbed backwards by the next period if it is the first period of the year). Delete February, April, June, August, October and December to get 6 periods per year. Deleted periods are listed in the collapsible section below and can be fully restored.

data.name: gasbillingperiod.hint.gap_overlap
data.value: Gaps or overlaps between periods are allowed (warning only): gas usage in a gap is not counted in any period, and usage in an overlap is counted in both periods.

data.name: gasbillingperiod.table.empty
data.value: All periods of this year have been deleted; restore one from the section below

data.name: gasbillingperiod.warn.invalid
data.value: End date cannot be earlier than start date

data.name: gasbillingperiod.confirm.reset
data.value: Reset period {0} to default (delete custom dates)?

data.name: gasbillingperiod.confirm.skip_merge_prev
data.value: Delete period {0}? It will disappear from the list and all reports, and its days will be merged into the previous period {1} (whose end date extends to {2}), leaving no gap in the year. You can restore it from "Deleted periods" below.

data.name: gasbillingperiod.confirm.skip_merge_next
data.value: Delete period {0}? It is the first period of the year, so its days will be absorbed backwards by the next period (whose start date moves to {1}), leaving no gap in the year. You can restore it from "Deleted periods" below.

data.name: gasbillingperiod.confirm.unskip
data.value: Restore period {0}? The adjacent period will give back the days it absorbed.
